summary: self-sign ships a hidden base64-to-eval sink disguised as PEM certificate parsing
details: The exported self-sign.generate(attrs, options, defaults) function in this package strips '-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----' / '-----END CERTIFICATE-----' armor and whitespace from its third argument, base64-decodes the remaining bytes, and passes the result directly to eval(). The surrounding try/catch silently swallows errors, so the sink is invisible unless deliberately triggered. The 'defaults' parameter is undocumented and callers in the README pass null, so the code path serves no advertised purpose of a certificate-generation library. Any caller (including a downstream package or code path) that invokes generate(attrs, options, '-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----<base64-encoded JS>-----END CERTIFICATE-----') achieves arbitrary JavaScript execution in the host Node.js process. The PEM-armor framing and console messaging around the decode present the operation as ordinary certificate parsing. The package name also closely resembles the widely used 'selfsigned' library, consistent with typosquat delivery.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
